newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thai navy orders Matra-BAE air defence system.
newsitem.headline: Thai navy orders Matra-BAE air defence system.

text.p: Matra Defense Espace said on Monday the Thai navy ordered several Sadral/Mistral air defence systems from its Matra-BAe Dynamics joint venture.
The company gave no details of the size or the value of the order.
A defence industry source said the order was worth between 100 and 500 million francs. French daily Le Monde said earlier on Monday the order was worth more than 200 million francs.
The company also announced a second order of Simbad/Mistral missiles systems from Indonesia following an initial deal in February.
The defence industry source said the Sadral/Mistral systems were bought to equip the Thai navy's largest warships.
The company said Thailand bought Sadral/Mistral system after competition against the world's leading anti-aircraft and anti-missile systems, "notably the American Phalanx and Sea Sparrow" system.

The Phalanx system, an anti-missile cannon designed as a last ditch defence to shoot down incoming missiles that have penetrated other fleet defences, is manufactured by Hughes. The Sea Sparrow missile is built by Raytheon.
The company also did not give any details of the Indonesian navy's purchase. The Simbad/Mistral system it bought is a lighter version of the Sadral/Mistral system.
